LESSON: FOOD ETIQUETTE

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES
Strand: Foods
Topic 3.2: Food Etiquette

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Food Etiquette
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Which are the good table learner should be able to: table manners (eating with mouth manners?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify good table manners to closed, not talking while eating, not 2.
2. practice good table manners hands before eating, not picking nose or when taking meals, teeth while at the table, not stretching

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Food Etiquette

Teach
• Observe Food Etiquette in real life (school compound, home, farm).
• Use safe examples only.
• Name → explain → apply.

Worked example
• Fact 1 about Food Etiquette (in pupil words).
• Fact 2 with a Kenyan example.
• Safe action connected to Food Etiquette.

Try this
• Draw/label one diagram for Food Etiquette.
• Write 5 bullet facts about Food Etiquette.
• Say one safety rule.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• identify good table manners to closed, not talking while eating, not 2.
• practice good table manners hands before eating, not picking nose or when taking meals, teeth while at the table, not stretching

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. List 8 facts on Food Etiquette.
2. Teach a friend using only bullet points.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet for Food Etiquette: meaning, diagram, 5 practice questions.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which are the good table learner should be able to: table manners (eating with mouth manners?
2. How should we behave observe when taking meals, placing elbow on the table, washing when taking meals?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• identify good table manners to closed, not talking while eating, not 2.
• practice good table manners hands before eating, not picking nose or when taking meals, teeth while at the table, not stretching

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
